JUDGMENT
The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that was occurred on 19.09.2024.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 19.09.2024 at about 2.15 p.m., the petitioner was riding his motorcycle bearing No.KA.42.ED.6436 along with his brother as pillion rider from Andrahalli main road to Nagaraholenagara, next to D group arch road to go to his house, and when the petitioner reached near Pradanamanthri Janaoushadhi Kendra, 2nd cross,
Vinayakanagara, and at that time the driver of the Car bearing No.KA.05.NL.6637 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed against the Motorcycle.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Meditech Hospital,
Andrahalli, after first aid treatment he was shifted to Suresh Hospital, Hegganahalli cross, Bengaluru wherein petitioner took treatment as an inpatient and treated conservatively and discharged with an advice for bed rest with regular follow up treatment for six months.
The petitioner has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- amount towards medical expenses other than towards conveyance, food and nourishment charges and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was aged about 24 years, working as Field worker at Manapuram Finance, Bengaluru and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner became permanently disabled and lost his earning capacity.
The respondent No.1 is the owner, respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
prays to award compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of summons the respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels and filed separate written statements.

sentences.text: The respondent No.1 -owner of the offending car has filed written statement by denying all the averments of the petition.
It has contended that the car bearing No.KA- 05-NL-6637 is insured with the second respondent and it was in force as on the date of accident.
Further this respondent has submitted that the driver of the said had valid driving licences as on the date of accident.
It has admitted that it is the owner of the car bearing No.KA- 05-NL-6637.
Further contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence and carelessness of the petitioner and not due to the driver of car bearing No.KA- 05-NL-6637.
Further it has denied the cause and manner of accident, the petitioner's age, occupation, income and injuries suffered by him.
By contending the negligence of the petitioner, prays to dismiss the petition against it.

After service of summons, the respondent No.2- insurance company appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by admitting issuance of policy in respect of the car bearing No.KA-05-NL-6637.

Further it has denied the cause and manner of accident, the petitioner's age,
occupation, income and injuries suffered by him.
Further contended that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
Further contended that the driver of the car was not having valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
It has also contended that petitioner was riding his motorcycle without observing moving vehicles on the road and also he had no driving licence and not wearing helmets .
Further it has contended that in fact the alleged motorcycle was ridden by petitioner's brother and he is not a pillion rider.
Further it has denied the cause and manner of accident, the petitioner's age, occupation, income and injuries suffered by him.
By denying the negligence of the offending Car bearing No.KA.05.NL.6637 the respondent No.2 prays to dismiss the claim petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of Car bear- ing Reg.No.KA-05-NL-6637 by its driver, in RTA took place on 19.09.2024 at about 2:15 p.m near Pradanamatri Jan Aushadhi Centre, Vinayaka Nagar, 2nd cross, Bengaluru?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
3 . What order or award?

The respondent No.1 examined its Manager as RW1 and got marked 4 documents at Ex.R1 to R4.
Initially the respondent No.1 owner examined its official as RW1.
Thereafter when the case is pending for cross- examination of RW1, the RW1 has left the office of respondent No.1 as such the new authorized person examined as RW2 as per order dated 21.01.2026.
No evidence is placed by the respondent No.2 insurance company.

Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

sentences.text: 19. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 19.09.2024 which was caused by the driver of the Car bearing No.KA.05.NL.6637 which belongs to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
20.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which was caused by the driver of the Car bearing No.KA.05.NL.6637.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
a) PAIN AND AGONY:-
At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 24 years.
As per Aadhaar card and DL marked at Ex.P11 and 12 the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 31.10.1999.
The accident was took place on 19.09.2024.
Hence as on the date of accident the petitioner was aged about 24 years 10 months 19 days.
The petitioner has produced wound certificate marked at Ex.P8.

As per Ex.P8 the petitioner was admitted to Suresh Hospital, Bengaluru wherein petitioner took treatment as an inpatient and underwent conservative treatment and has sustained swelling over right knee and ligamental tear of right knee.
By considering the nature of injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.30,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.
b) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bill as per Ex.P14 amounting to Rs.11,083/- which are supported by medical prescription at Ex.P13.
The medical bills are not seriously disputed by the respondents and no grounds are made out to disbelieve these bill.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitled for the reimbursement of the same by rounding off the same i.e., Rs. 11,100/-.
c) Loss of income during laid up period:
The petitioner has stated that he was a working as Field worker at Mannapuram Finance, Bengaluru and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
The petitioner has stated that he was doing Field work at Manapuram Finance, Bengaluru and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.

To prove the said fact the petitioner has produced the account statement which shows that on 31.07.2024 the petitioner has got salary of Rs.23,700/-, the same is taken from Manapuram Finance and the same is taken as income of the petitioner.
The petitioner pleaded that he was admitted to Suresh Hospital, but no discharge summary is produced in this regard.

sentences.text: After injury usually the healing period has to be considered for which in the absence of evidence, this court is of the opinion that in total 2 months period may be considered under this head as a loss of income.

So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.23,700 X 2 months =
Rs.47,400/- during the laid up period.
d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him the petitioner has examined Dr.
Nagaraj B.N., Orthopaedic Surgeon as PW.2
and through him clinical notes, X-rays were got marked at Ex.P17 and Ex.P18.
According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained right ligamentous injury with complete tear of the ACL.
As per the evidence of PW2 doctor the petitioner sustained right lower limb disability of 40% and whole body disability of 13%.
This aspect is not impeached during the course of cross-examination.
The disability caused to the petitioner may affect on his occupation to some extent.
In the cross-examination PW2 stated that the injuries are healed and the petitioner can do his day to day activities with some difficulties.
It is pleaded that the petitioner was working as a Field work at Manapuram finance.
When the IA was filed by seeking direction to produce the account statement of the petitioner the same was produced which shows that till the date of accident the petitioner got the salary.
In the field work the usage of lower limbs has greater impact.

A perusal of the injuries sustained, treatment taken, it is considered that the injury of right ligamentous injury with complete tear of the ACL has greater impact over the functional disability of the petitioner.
Hence considering all these aspects this tribunal has taken disability at 6%.
The petitioner has stated that he was doing Field work at Manapuram Finance, Bengaluru and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.

To prove the said fact the petitioner has produced the account statement which shows that on 31.07.2024 the petitioner has got salary of Rs.23,700/-, the same is taken from Manapuram Finance and the same is taken as income of the petitioner.
As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '18'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.23,700/- X 12 X 18 X 6% =Rs.3,07,152/- which is the total loss of future income.
e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE; As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P8 the petitioner has sustained simple as well as grievous injury.
By considering the nature of the injury and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.

Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injury sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.

21. Liability:-
According to the petitioner the respondent No.1 & 2 are the owner and insurer of the Car bearing No.KA.05.NL.6637.

Even though the respondent No.2 in its objection statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the Car bearing No.KA.05.NL.6637, no evidence is placed by the respondent No.2 insurance company to eschew their liability.
No other grounds are made out by showing the contributory negligence of the petitioner or violation of policy conditions by the respondent No.1 owner.
Hence the Respondent No.2 insurance company is liable to indemnify the liability of respondent No.1- owner.

The petitioner is entitled for the interest @ 6%
p.a.
Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
22.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.4,35,652/- (Rupees Four lakhs thirty five thousand six hundred fifty two only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.2- insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of the amount awarded, it is ordered to release the entire compensation amount to the petitioner.
